episodes.180432: A line of showers and thunderstorms produced a marine wind gust in Galveston Bay.
episodes.180440: Scattered thunderstorms occurred during the afternoon or evening, an isolated severe one produced some wind damage.
episodes.180445: Thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain in southeastern Pennsylvania on the afternoon of July 7. Rainfall totals were as high as 2.0 to 3.5 inches.
episodes.180477: The combination of a disturbance over CO along with healthy low-level moisture resulted in severe storms developing across the eastern plains of New Mexico. These cells produced quarter sized hail at times. Cells congealed into squall lines as they approached the Texas border resulting in severe wind gusts.
episodes.180511: Strong thunderstorms pushing offshore produced strong wind gusts along the Brevard and Indian River coasts.
episodes.180524: Scattered storms formed ahead of an approaching cold front during the afternoon and evening of July 6, 2023. A few of the cells merged to form a short-lived line that produced sporadic wind damage and a measured gust to 58 mph at Williamsport Regional Airport.
episodes.180525: Scattered showers and storms developed from the Susquehanna Valley into northeastern Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening of July 7, 2023.  One storm produced a bit of wind damage in upper Dauphin County.
episodes.180776: A weak upper level trough extended southwest from the Great Lakes Region southwest into Southwest Arkansas and Northeast Texas during the afternoon of July 6th, which reinforced a weak surface front south into the I-30 corridor of Northeast Texas and Southern Arkansas. Meanwhile, a strong seabreeze pushed inland across East Texas and North Louisiana during the late afternoon through the evening hours, allowing showers and thunderstorms to spread north into these areas. Strong daytime heating and large scale ascent along the slow moving front contributed to the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms along and south of the front across portions of East Texas and North Louisiana, and collided with the northward advancing storms associated with the seabreeze during the late afternoon and early evening hours, with a cluster of showers and thunderstorms redeveloping over the same areas from Harrison County Texas into Southern Caddo and Bossier Parishes in Northwest Louisiana. Given the very moist air mass in place, these slow moving storms were efficient rainfall producers, contributing to areas of flash flooding that were observed over these locations. Localized pockets of 2-5 inch rains fell over far South Shreveport and Southern Caddo Parish in a short period of time, with multiple roads flooded before the storms diminished by mid and late evening.
episodes.180817: Severe thunderstorms moved over the northern Nebraska Panhandle from east-central Wyoming on the evening of the 6th producing quarter size hail and strong winds near Harrison.
episodes.180818: Severe thunderstorms developed over east-central Wyoming late in the afternoon on the 6th tracking southeast producing large hail near Lusk and strong winds near Douglas.
episodes.180820: A cold front passed through the area on the 7th, leading to a few showers and thunderstorms. Some thunderstorms caused heavy rainfall in a short period of time that led to isolated instances of flooding and flash flooding in northern Virginia.
episodes.180821: A cold front passed through the area on the 7th, leading to a few showers and thunderstorms. Some thunderstorms caused heavy rainfall in a short period of time that led to an instance of flooding.
episodes.181263: An upper level high pressure system over El Paso was being partially suppressed by a short wave moving across northern New Mexico on the evening of the seventh. Scattered thunderstorms developed along a surface pressure trough near the Texas/New Mexico state line and drifted eastward during the late afternoon and evening hours as a broken line of thunderstorms. Hot and dry near surface conditions allowed for high cloud bases supporting severe wind gusts underneath thunderstorm activity. Several Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet sites measured severe wind gusts with the strongest activity.
episodes.181531: A cold front supported scattered showers and thunderstorms across Central New York. Multiple storms became severe with damaging wind gusts being the main threat. Minor damage of downed trees and wires was reported across the region.
episodes.181532: A cold front supported scattered showers and thunderstorms across Northeastern Pennsylvania. Multiple storms became severe with damaging wind gusts being the main threat. Minor damage of downed trees and wires was reported across the region.
episodes.181709: Westerly flow and a warm, unstable airmass triggered strong to isolated severe pulse storms during the afternoon and evening when sea breezes and boundaries collided. Storms drifted toward the Atlantic coast into the early evening.
episodes.181710: Westerly flow and a warm, unstable airmass triggered strong to isolated severe pulse storms during the afternoon and evening when sea breezes and boundaries collided. Storms drifted toward the Atlantic coast into the early evening.
episodes.181869: Unstable air along a pressure trough well ahead of a cold front over the Ohio River Valley sparked scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours. Localized wind damage was reported in northern Maryland, and a considerably severe thunderstorm affected parts of the central Shenandoah Valley in Virginia.
episodes.181870: A pressure trough sparked several thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours, a few of which produced localized wind damage east of the Blue Ridge and Catoctin Mountains.
episodes.181871: A pressure trough sparked several thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours, a few of which produced localized wind damage east of the Blue Ridge and Catoctin Mountains.
episodes.181937: A thunderstorm produced localized gale-force wind gusts over the middle tidal Potomac River.
episodes.181977: Convection developed during the day and was enhanced by the sea breeze. The storms intensified briefly to severe limits before weakening near the coast late in the evening.
episodes.181978: Convection developed during the day and was enhanced by the sea breeze. The storms intensified briefly to severe limits before weakening near the coast late in the evening.
episodes.182022: Clusters of showers and thunderstorms crossed the Green Mountain state on July 7, 2023. Torrential downpours were frequent with some storms repeatedly training over the southern and central Green Mountains as well in portions of northeastern Vermont where, in some cases, considerable flash flooding occurred.
episodes.182037: Several clusters of training showers and thunderstorms, some with torrential rainfall affected portions of Clinton County, NY on the afternoon of July 7, 2023. Areas around Altona, NY and Dannemora, NY were affected by flash flooding after several inches of rain was observed.
episodes.182111: An upper level disturbance in westerly winds aloft helped to intensify storms over the High Plains and carry these storms east during the night of July 6th and into the morning hours of July 7th. Instability had increased across central and south central Nebraska during the overnight period. A line of thunderstorms had moved across central Nebraska during the early morning hours of July 7th. This line of storms moved through Polk County around 8 AM CDT. The front end and strongest part of the line of storms had already moved through the area when lightning struck a grain elevator on the northeastern fringe of the town of Shelby. Six employees who were working on the construction of the grain elevator were sent to the hospital with non-life threatening injuries due to the lightning strike.
episodes.182134: A slow moving cold front dropped through south central North Dakota and the James River Valley during the afternoon hours. Strong low level instability combined with converging winds along the frontal boundary resulting in multiple landspout tornadoes developing. All three of the reported tornadoes touched down in open fields and impacted no structures, thus there was no damage to evaluate. Therefore, by National Weather Service policy, all the landspout tornadoes were rated EF Unknown. In addition to the tornadoes, there were two reports of hail. The largest hail reported was one-inch in diameter and fell in McIntosh County.
episodes.182166: On the morning of the 7th, a robust mesoscale convective system (MCS) entered portions of northwestern Oklahoma and translated towards central Oklahoma through mid-morning hours. A corridor of wind damage and one tornado occurred across Woodward County due to a mesovortex. Elsewhere, intermittent increases in storm intensity lead to reports and measurements of severe-caliber wind and small hail. Brief training of heavy thunderstorm cores also lead to street flooding near the community of Kingfisher.||During the evening hours of the 7th, an additional MCS developed across the Texas Panhandle and entered western Oklahoma. Once again, wind damage occurred with the most intense portions of the thunderstorm line. This included a report of extensive wind damage near Foss State Park in Custer County.
episodes.182310: A Piedmont trough was the focus of initially isolated thunderstorms during the mid afternoon. The storms formed over the eastern Piedmont, then became more clustered as they moved southeast and south through portions of Edgecombe, Wilson, Franklin, Wake, Wilson, Nash, Wayne, Harnett, Johnston, and Sampson Counties.
episodes.182726: Severe thunderstorms in North Dakota and Minnesota led to hail and funnel cloud reports across the area.
episodes.182915: Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms developed amid a warm and humid air mass ahead of an approaching cold front on July 7, 2023. Some storms became severe downing trees and powerlines. Locally heavy rainfall also resulted in some instances of street flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.182917: Thunderstorms developed along a cold front in north-central South Dakota during the afternoon hours of July 7th. Quarter-size hail was observed near Hillsview in McPherson County.
episodes.182952: A slow moving cold front produced scattered showers and some thunderstorms. One of these storms was strong enough to produce isolated severe winds with a few trees downed near the town of South Butler.
episodes.182997: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.183006: A typical summer pattern prevailed with scattered thunderstorms producing occasional gusty winds across the coastal waters.
episodes.183044: A late evening thunderstorm dropped south into eastern Buckingham County. This severe thunderstorm produced damaging winds that brought down numerous trees and powerlines.
episodes.183062: During the early morning hours of the 7th, a storm complex impacted portions of Kansas, western Oklahoma, and the far northeastern combined OK/TX Panhandle. This complex impacted Beaver County with 62 to 82 mph winds and heavy rain.
episodes.183063: During the late afternoon of the 7th a line of thunderstorms developed in eastern New Mexico and proceeded to move east into and across the combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles. The strongest and most severe of these storms mainly impacted the TX Panhandle as it progressed. Several severe wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph winds were measured by ground stations across the area. Some of the strongest parts of the storms even produced some heavy rainfall.
episodes.183080: A cold front moved into the area, sparking a few showers and thunderstorms. One of those storms ended up being severe, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.183257: Severe thunderstorms produced very large hail in Lincoln County, ranging from 1 to 4 inches in diameter.  At least one spotter reported extensive hail damage to their home when it was struck by baseball size hail.  In  addition, two landspout tornadoes were observed in Adams and Arapahoe Counties.  One of the tornadoes picked up a 1400 pound disk and tossed it approximately 100 yards.
episodes.183258: A squall line developed in the central and northern Sandhills during the late night of July 6 and early morning of July 7, resulting in strong to severe winds.
episodes.183343: Almost three inches of rain dumped in Monticello (Drew County) on the 6th, and high water flowed across Highway 278. The road had to be closed temporarily. It was the same story at Greenbrier (Faulkner County), with numerous roads under water.
episodes.183353: Thunderstorms developed in advance of a cold front crossing the region during the afternoon of the 7th. Slow moving and training thunderstorms across the higher terrain of Baxter State Park produced heavy rain which led to localized flash flooding. Flash flooding developed along the Nesowadnehunk Stream. The Park Tote Road was covered with 8 to 10 inches of running water. The road was closed for several hours until the flash flooding subsided.
episodes.183354: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours of July 6th, in an environment characterized by 800 to 1000 J/kg of downdraft CAPE.  This, plus sufficient dry air aloft, allowed for the development of downburst winds that produced isolated instances of wind damage.
episodes.183430: A cold front supported scattered heavy rain-producing thunderstorms across Northeastern Pennsylvania. Multiple storms moved very slowly over the same townships of Lackawanna, Wayne and Pike counties. A very small area of 3 to 5 inches of rainfall triggered flooding of roads and a local business.
episodes.183434: A cold front supported scattered heavy rain-producing thunderstorms across Central New York. Multiple storms formed over the same locations, providing parts of the region with excessive amounts between 2 to 4 inches.
episodes.183451: A mesoscale convective vortex moved through weak west-northwest flow aloft over the Lower Mississippi Valley and triggered a round of showers and thunderstorms across northeast Arkansas and the Missouri Bootheel during the evening hours of July 6, 2023. There were a few damaging wind reports.
episodes.183452: A mesoscale convective vortex moved through weak west-northwest flow aloft over the Lower Mississippi Valley and triggered a round of showers and thunderstorms across northeast Arkansas and the Missouri Bootheel during the evening hours of July 6, 2023. There were a few damaging wind reports.
episodes.183476: From the afternoon of July 6 on into the evening, isolated to scattered clusters of showers and thunderstorms impacted portions of northern Utah and southwest Wyoming, yielding a few strong to severe wind gusts.
episodes.183631: Clusters of strong thunderstorms developed across portions of southeast Georgia and southeast South Carolina during the afternoon and early evening hours. These thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the coast.
episodes.183632: A strong thunderstorm developed in Bulloch County in the afternoon and tracked to the southeast. The thunderstorm produced significant wind damage in the Brooklet area.
episodes.183714: Thunderstorms produced large hail and damaging winds across far southwestern Kansas.
episodes.183767: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with low pressure and a surface trough produced damaging winds across portions of central Virginia.
episodes.183768: Scattered thunderstorms associated with low pressure and a surface trough produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of central Virginia.
episodes.183769: Scattered thunderstorms associated with low pressure and a surface trough produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore.
episodes.183770: Isolated severe thunderstorm associated with low pressure and a surface trough produced damaging winds across portions of northeast North Carolina.
episodes.183791: A slow moving frontal boundary triggers shower and thunderstorms with heavy rainfall on the afternoon of the 7th. The anomalously humid airmass resulted in torrential rainfall rates around 2 to 3 inches per hour and localized flooding across the mountains of western Maine.
episodes.183942: A shortwave moved across Wyoming. As it encountered more humid air east of the Bighorn Range, severe thunderstorms developed in Johnson and Natrona Counties. There were numerous reports of hail from nickel to golf ball size hail, including on Interstate 25 which slowed traffic for a time. In portions of Fremont and Sweetwater Counties, strong winds mixed to the surface and brought local high wind.
episodes.184057: A hot and humid summertime environment triggered pulse storms to form over southern Mississippi. A particular cluster formed over coastal Mississippi and propagated over the waters during the night of July 6th.
episodes.184058: Marine convection formed overnight in a typical diurnal convective pattern. One strong storm developed strong downburst winds before dissipating after sunrise.
episodes.184060: A weak frontal boundary moved across a moderately unstable airmass across the Champlain Valley of New York. This allowed for the development of showers and scattered thunderstorms, some of which produced damaging winds.
episodes.184063: A weak frontal boundary moved across a moderately to strong unstable airmass across Vermont. This allowed for the development of showers and scattered thunderstorms, some of which produced damaging winds and flash flooding.
episodes.184075: Daytime heating fueled several strong to marginally severe storms across the area on both the afternoon/evening of July 7th and 8th. The hardest hit areas were across parts of east-central GA, around the town of Jefferson (Jackson County) and also over southern Oglethorpe county (July 8th).
episodes.184126: Residual moisture from an incredibly anomalously wet June continues to moisten the lower levels aiding in ample amounts of instability. The northwest flow pattern created a lot of shear, which led to prolonged 3 day severe weather event over adjacent and eastern plains of southern Colorado.
episodes.184155: A slow moving upper level disturbance interacted with deep moisture over south Texas to produce thunderstorms over the inland Coastal Bend during the early morning hours of the 7th. Thunderstorms producing locally heavy rainfall remained over the inland Coastal Bend for several hours. Rainfall amounts ranged from 4 to 8 inches from north of Alice southwest to near Benavides. This caused flooding of roads near and south of San Diego.
episodes.184865: A line of strong thunderstorms impacted the inland rivers, sounds, and coastal waters along the Crystal Coast during the evening hours on July 7th. Thunderstorms brought strong wind gusts to the area.
episodes.185215: Scattered storms developed during the afternoon and a few storms became strong.
